about.title: South San Francisco Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: South San Francisco's economy runs on biotech labs, distribution centers, and industrial sites clustered near US-101 and Grand Avenue, and injuries on these job sites are common — falls, forklift accidents, chemical exposure, and repetitive strain among them. In California, workers' compensation is typically the exclusive remedy against your own employer, no matter who was at fault, but that doesn't end the story. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, delivery driver, or property owner outside your employer contributed to the accident, you may have a separate third-party injury claim worth pursuing alongside your workers' comp benefits. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free service that connects injured South San Francisco workers with an independent attorney who can review both angles of a case and explain what's realistic, without pressure or upfront cost.

whyChoose.title: Why South San Francisco Workers Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: We Look Beyond Workers' Comp
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker can still be held liable. An attorney can help sort out whether that applies to your situation.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter
items.desc: California generally requires injured workers to report an incident to their employer within 30 days, so timing matters from day one. We can help you get matched with someone who explains the process clearly.

items.title: Retaliation Is Illegal
items.desc: It's against California law for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting an injury or filing a claim. An independent attorney can advise you on your rights if you're worried about your job.

items.question: I was hurt at a biotech facility near Grand Avenue. Can I still file a workers' comp claim and a separate lawsuit?
items.answer: Possibly. Workers' comp usually covers your employer regardless of fault, but if a contractor, equipment supplier, or another company outside your employer contributed to the injury, a separate third-party claim may be available. An independent attorney can review the details of your South San Francisco workplace accident and explain your options.

items.question: What's the deadline to report a workplace injury in California?
items.answer: Generally, you should notify your employer within 30 days of the injury. Missing that window can complicate your workers' comp claim, so it's best to report as soon as possible and get medical documentation.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for reporting an injury?
items.answer: No, retaliation for reporting a workplace injury or filing a claim is illegal under California law. If you believe you've faced retaliation, an independent attorney connected through LawProactive can help you understand your next steps.
